pages.text: Neither melts out of its ore in a furnace. Sphalerite is zinc sulfide, and roasts to zinc oxide only in a heated basin with 500 mB of air, giving off its sulfur as sulfur dioxide; smithsonite and hemimorphite, the old calamine, calcine to it on a fire.
pages.title: Zinc

pages.text: Zinc boils at 907 °C, below the heat that reduces it, so it was distilled from a sealed retort packed with charcoal: a zinc oxide and a charcoal in a basin over a blaze burner fed a blaze cake give a zinc ingot.

Cadmium boils at 767 °C and comes over first, so one retort in ten also gives a cadmium sponge: Stromeyer found the element in 1817 in calamine. Asurine, the zinc stone, crushes to smithsonite. Zinc oxide is also what every sulfur cure of rubber needs to work, so the Factory's rubber takes one.
Since the 1910s most zinc has been won in water instead: roasted, leached in sulfuric acid and electrowon, and now nine tenths of it is (Sinclair, The Extractive Metallurgy of Zinc).
pages.title: Electrolytic zinc

pages.text: Two zinc oxide, 500 mB of sulfuric acid and 500 mB of water in a heated vat with a mixer give 1,000 mB of zinc leach liquor, and one leach in five leaves a zinc leach residue, the ferrite and lead sulfate that hold the germanium and indium.

The copper, cobalt and cadmium in the liquor would foul the cathode, so it is stirred hot with a zinc nugget, zinc dust that cements them out: 1,000 mB of zinc sulfate liquor, and one batch in five a cadmium sponge. 500 mB of that on two electrodes in a vat give a zinc ingot and 250 mB of sulfuric acid back to the leach.

The purification comes out in its order: copper first, as a copper cement that a blast furnace fire-refines to a copper ingot; then cobalt, as a cobalt cake that 250 mB of sulfuric acid, heated, turn to cobalt sulfate; then cadmium.
pages.title: What else is in the liquor

pages.text: Manganese in the liquor plates out on the anodes as anode mud, MnO2, one cell in twenty, which a coke and 500 mB of sulfuric acid, heated, turn to two manganese sulfate.
The roaster gas carries the ore's mercury, scrubbed out as calomel by the Boliden-Norzink process one roast in twenty; a calomel and a limesand, heated, give mercury back.
The leach residue is mostly zinc ferrite, which a neutral leach cannot touch.
pages.title: Jarosite

pages.text: Two of it with 500 mB of sulfuric acid and 100 mB of ammonia in a heated vat give 500 mB more zinc leach liquor, a jarosite and a lead-silver residue: the jarosite process of 1965, which drops the iron as ammonium jarosite (Arregui, Gordon and Steintveit, 1980).

The lead-silver residue goes to a lead smelter; in a bloomery it gives lead bullion and a slag. The jarosite, holding lead, arsenic and cadmium, is impounded in lined ponds: nine pack into a jarosite pond.

Half the world's zinc goes on steel (International Zinc Association). Dipped in molten zinc at about 450 °C, steel takes a coat that corrodes in its place and, scratched through, still goes before the steel does.
pages.title: Galvanizing

pages.text: Four heavy plates and a zinc nugget, heated, give four galvanized steel plates, which do anything a steel plate does and never rust; a bare heavy plate rusts as a steel ingot does.

Carbon does not part nickel from iron: it reduces both, and they alloy. Pentlandite roasted on a fire and smelted with a charcoal, superheated, gives a ferronickel ingot and a slag, and whatever platinum it carried is lost in it.
pages.title: Ferronickel

pages.text: Nickel laterite, a weathered rock of 1.5 to 2.5 per cent nickel, is smelted whole: four of it with two charcoal, superheated, give one ferronickel and two slag, as the rotary kilns and electric furnaces of New Caledonia and Indonesia smelt it at about 1,550 °C.

Real ferronickel runs 20 to 40 per cent nickel, and nickel pig iron less (Crundwell and others, Extractive Metallurgy of Nickel, Cobalt and Platinum Group Metals, 2011); here an ingot is a third nickel. None of it is ever nickel metal.
pages.title: Nickel

pages.text: It goes where two thirds of the world's nickel goes, into stainless steel, which wants the iron anyway: three ferrochrome, three ferronickel and four steel, superheated, make ten stainless. Nickel metal comes from sulfide matte: leached and electrowon, under the platinum metals, or by Mond's carbonyl.
